\section[bewerben]{bewerben — to apply (sich bewerben)}

\label{lesson:GE-C177-bewerben}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the German for to describe, then the German for to enter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: bewerben}
\textbf{bewerben} — \textquotedblleft{}to apply (sich bewerben)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{bewerben} is \emph{be-} + the verb \textquotedblleft{}to recruit, to woo\textquotedblright{}, Old High German \emph{werban} $\leftarrow$ Proto-Germanic \emph{*hwerbaną}, \textquotedblleft{}to turn\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1). To apply is to court a post.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[buchstabieren]{buchstabieren — to spell}

\label{lesson:GE-C177-buchstabieren}



\begin{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: buchstabieren}
\textbf{buchstabieren} — \textquotedblleft{}to spell\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{buchstabieren} is built on the word for \textquotedblleft{}a letter of the alphabet\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}beech staff\textquotedblright{}, commonly explained by the beech staves runes were carved on, + the ending \emph{-ieren}.
\end{cousinweb}
